text:
alex: Heads up — I'm seeing missing child spans from the async prefetcher in prod. Root request traces show end-to-end but worker spans not present. Anyone seen this pattern?
marie: Are logs showing any errors? Which service + sample trace id?
sam: Could be OTEL batch exporter + process crash; or context not propagated into goroutine. Do we use tracer.StartSpan in goroutine or Start(ctx)?
alex: service: prefetcher-v2, trace id: 7f3a9c2b... Logs have no errors, just completion messages. Prefetcher runs as background goroutine via workqueue.
sam: Quick grep tip — search for "context.Background()" and instances of creating a new TracerProvider. If TP is created per-request spans never make it to exporter.
alex: We do pass ctx into the goroutine but I remembered a helper that uses context.Background() for timeouts, will check.
infra-bot: Dashboard quick link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/obs/traces?panel=prefetcher-overview — filter by service=prefetcher-v2
marie: Also check that you're not calling span.End() in the parent before work completes. Common pattern bug.
sam: Also consider sampler: if parent sampling decision is false child spans won't be exported. For debugging set OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=always_on locally or in the canary.
alex: Pasting the small snippet we use now:
```
ctx, span := tracer.Start(ctx, "prefetch_job")
go func() {
  defer span.End()
  doWork(ctx)
}()
```
marie: There's the issue — you're ending the span in the parent while the child goroutine is still running. Move the span creation into the goroutine or end in the goroutine. Example:
```
go func(ctx context.Context){
  ctx, span := tracer.Start(ctx, "prefetch_job")
  defer span.End()
  doWork(ctx)
}(ctx)
```
sam: Good catch. Also double-check batch/span-processor exporter flush config on process shutdown. If the worker is short-lived the exporter might not flush. Batching + short lived spans = lost spans.
alex: Makes sense. I'll fix the span location + force always_on on canary to verify.
marie: While you test, add a temporary alert: prefetcher spans/minute drops >50% vs 1h baseline and exporter_errors > 0. Grafana panels to watch: traces count, spans/sec, exporter errors, span duration p95. I'll drop the dashboard links in #observability after lunch.
alex: Thanks — opening a PR now with the change and a canary rollout. Will ping when deployed. :thumbsup:
sam: If you want I can join a quick pairing session to validate traces after canary deploy.
alex: Appreciated, ping me in-thread or DM.
